explain.say: Imagine your best friend failed a test and was crying. Would you say, "You are useless"? Of course not! So why do we sometimes say that to ourselves? Being kind to yourself is called self-compassion. Look at the plan. Step one: notice it hurts.

faq.a: Self-compassion means treating yourself with the same kindness you would show a good friend, especially when you make a mistake or feel bad.
asks: What does being kind to yourself mean?

faq.q: How do I talk kindly to myself?
faq.a: Imagine what you would say to a friend in the same situation, then say it to yourself. Swap "I am useless" for "That was hard, and I can try again."
asks: How do I stop being mean to myself?

faq.q: Does giving myself a hug really help?
faq.a: Gentle touch, even your own, like a hand on your heart, can help your body feel calmer and safer. It is a quick, private way to comfort yourself.

faq.q: Is being kind to myself the same as being lazy?
faq.a: No. Research shows that people who are kind to themselves after failing often work harder next time, because they are not frozen by fear of failing.

faq.q: Why am I so hard on myself?
faq.a: It can come from wanting to do well, from habit, or from unkind things you have heard. Being hard on yourself is a habit, and habits can change with practice.
asks: Why do I always criticise myself?

facts: Psychologist Kristin Neff describes self-compassion as three parts: kindness to yourself, remembering everyone struggles, and noticing your feelings calmly.
In a 2012 study, students who were encouraged to be kind to themselves after failing a test studied longer for the next one.
